questions.text: Money market deals mainly with:
options: Short-term funds and instruments with maturity less than 1 year
questions.explanation: Money market instruments such as T-Bills, CPs and CDs have maturities below one year.

questions.text: An unsecured loan is one that:
options: Has no underlying asset pledged to the lender
questions.explanation: Unsecured loans rely solely on borrower’s creditworthiness rather than collateral.

questions.text: Which ministry is responsible for macroeconomic policy and capital markets through its Department of Economic Affairs?
questions.explanation: The Ministry of Finance, via the Department of Economic Affairs, handles macroeconomic policy and capital markets.

questions.text: Which of the following would improve cash-flow position?
questions.explanation: Reducing discretionary outflows increases surplus.

questions.text: A 'risk-neutral' investor:
options: Demands the highest risk premium for all investments
Focuses only on expected return, ignoring risk
questions.explanation: A risk-neutral investor evaluates investments solely on expected returns without regard for risk.

questions.text: A perpetual bond (consol) is valued using the formula:
options: Price = Coupon / required rate of return
questions.explanation: For a perpetuity, Price = coupon per period divided by the required rate of return, since cash flows continue indefinitely.

questions.text: Budget variance occurs when:
options: Actual figures differ from budgeted figures
All bills are paid on time
questions.explanation: Variance = Actual − Budgeted; it helps monitor deviations.

questions.text: Psychographic analysis of an investor helps in:
options: Understanding behavioural traits and risk personality
questions.explanation: Psychographic analysis identifies behavioural and personality characteristics affecting investment decisions and risk profile.

questions.text: The formula for the Sharpe Ratio is:
options: (Portfolio Return – Risk-Free Rate) / Standard Deviation of Portfolio
questions.explanation: Sharpe Ratio = (Rp – Rf) / σp, where Rp is portfolio return, Rf is risk-free rate, and σp is portfolio’s standard deviation.

questions.text: Portfolio Managers can invest a maximum of ___% of a client’s portfolio in their own associate or related companies.
questions.explanation: As per SEBI, the cap is 30% with prior written consent from the client.

questions.text: Which regulator handles insurance-related investor complaints?
questions.explanation: IRDAI regulates insurance entities and handles insurance-related grievances.

questions.text: Category III AIFs are characterised by:
options: Use of diverse or complex trading strategies including leverage
questions.explanation: Category III AIFs, such as hedge funds, employ complex or leverage-based trading strategies and invest in listed or unlisted securities.

questions.text: A market order is an order to:
options: Buy or sell at a specified price
Buy or sell immediately at the best available price
questions.explanation: Market orders execute immediately at current best prices.

questions.text: The overarching ethical test for any adviser action is:
options: Will it pass regulatory scrutiny alone?
Is it legal, fair, transparent, and in the client’s best interest?
questions.explanation: Ethical actions must be legal, fair, transparent, and aligned with the client’s best interests and market integrity.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a category of AIF under SEBI regulations?
questions.explanation: There are only three categories of AIF — Category I, II and III.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is TRUE regarding investor grievance handling?
options: Complaints can only be submitted physically
SCORES allows paperless digital complaint resolution
Investors must pay a fee to file on SCORES
questions.explanation: SCORES provides a free, paperless, and transparent process for investors to submit and monitor complaints online.

questions.text: In an EMI, the interest component:
options: Is zero in the first year
questions.explanation: As principal outstanding reduces, the interest portion of each EMI declines.

questions.text: A client nearing retirement with a low risk appetite should:
options: Shift progressively from equity to fixed income and capital preservation assets
questions.explanation: As retirement nears, focus shifts to capital protection and stable income, reducing equity exposure.

questions.text: Category III AIFs may be open-ended or close-ended depending on:
questions.explanation: Category III AIFs can be open-ended or close-ended depending on their investment strategy and disclosure in the PPM.

questions.text: The key compliance requirement for all intermediaries under SEBI is:
options: Filing annual audit reports with SEBI
Maintaining client confidentiality and proper records
questions.explanation: Intermediaries must maintain confidentiality and records as part of SEBI’s code of conduct and inspection norms.

questions.text: Debt restructuring refers to:
options: Revising loan terms to make repayment easier
questions.explanation: It may involve extending tenure, reducing rate, or partial waiver to restore repayment ability.

questions.text: A client wanting to retire early at age 50 instead of 60 will generally need to:
options: Save more and invest more aggressively in earlier years
questions.explanation: Early retirement means fewer earning years and more retired years, requiring higher saving and often more growth-oriented investments.

questions.text: If the Sharpe Ratio of a portfolio is less than that of the market, it indicates:
options: Portfolio underperforms on a risk-adjusted basis
questions.explanation: A lower Sharpe Ratio than the market indicates inferior risk-adjusted performance.

questions.text: An investor’s holding in a mutual fund is represented by:
options: Number of shares of the AMC
Number of bonds issued by the scheme
Number of units of the scheme
Amount of cash in the trust account
questions.explanation: Each investor’s holding in a mutual fund is represented in terms of units of the scheme.

questions.text: Which of these best describes holistic financial planning?
options: Coordinating investments, insurance, tax, retirement and estate aspects around the client’s life goals
Keeping all money in a savings account
questions.explanation: Holistic planning considers all aspects of the client’s financial life and integrates them around their goals.

questions.text: A closed-end mutual fund scheme:
options: Is generally listed on a stock exchange to provide liquidity
Always allows redemption directly with the AMC
questions.explanation: Closed-end schemes are for a fixed term and are mandatorily listed on a stock exchange so investors can exit by selling units there.

questions.text: As the number of securities in a portfolio increases, the number of covariance terms:
questions.explanation: For n securities, the number of covariance terms is n(n–1)/2, which grows rapidly as portfolio size increases.

questions.text: Ethical investing primarily involves:
options: Investing in sin industries for profit
Selecting investments based on personal moral principles
questions.explanation: Ethical investing filters out investments conflicting with an investor’s moral or ethical beliefs, such as gambling or tobacco.

questions.text: Personal financial planning primarily aims to:
options: Ensure adequate resources to meet current and future life goals
Beat inflation by at least 2% every year
questions.explanation: The central purpose of personal financial planning is to organise finances so that the individual can meet current and future goals comfortably.

questions.text: A cash-flow deficit indicates that:
questions.explanation: Deficit means spending more than earnings; corrective action needed.

questions.text: In which stage of the financial life cycle does preservation of capital and regular income become more important than high growth?
questions.explanation: As individuals near retirement, their focus shifts to capital preservation and stable income.

questions.text: Who publishes daily reference rates for major currency pairs like USD/INR?
questions.explanation: FBIL publishes daily reference rates for key currency pairs on Mumbai business days.

questions.text: If a complaint remains unresolved even after arbitration, an investor may approach:
questions.explanation: Investors can approach Consumer Courts or High Courts if dissatisfied after arbitration.

questions.text: Which is an example of DIRECT investment by a retail investor?
options: Buying a diversified equity mutual fund
Investing through a PMS in multiple stocks
Buying listed shares of a company in her own demat account
Investing in a Category II AIF
questions.explanation: Buying shares directly in a demat account is a direct investment; mutual funds, PMS and AIFs are managed/pooled vehicles.

questions.text: Retirement funds and children’s funds launched by mutual funds are classified as:
questions.explanation: Retirement funds and children’s funds fall under SEBI’s solution-oriented scheme category and come with specified lock-in periods.

questions.text: Portfolio optimization requires estimation of which parameters?
options: Expected returns, standard deviations, and correlation coefficients
questions.explanation: Portfolio optimization requires estimates of expected returns, risk (standard deviation), and correlation between securities.

questions.text: A bond trades at a premium to face value when:
options: Coupon rate is equal to the current market yield
Coupon rate is higher than the current market yield
Coupon rate is lower than the current market yield
questions.explanation: If the bond’s coupon exceeds the market yield, investors are willing to pay more than face value, so the bond trades at a premium.

questions.text: Investors must update change in address or bank details:
questions.explanation: KYC-linked changes such as address and bank details must be updated with the KRA, which auto-updates all linked AMCs.

questions.text: Which of these steps improves credit score?
options: Timely payment of EMIs and credit-card bills
questions.explanation: Consistent on-time repayment and moderate utilisation boost score.

questions.text: Sustainable investing considers which key factors?
questions.explanation: Sustainable investing focuses on ESG—environmental, social, and governance—criteria for long-term positive impact.

questions.text: For mutual fund-related complaints, investors can also contact:
questions.explanation: AMFI assists investors in resolving mutual fund-related complaints in coordination with the concerned AMC.

questions.text: In the investor life cycle, the 'accumulation phase' is characterized by:
options: High net worth and focus on capital preservation
Building assets with higher risk tolerance and long horizon
questions.explanation: In the accumulation phase, investors are early in their careers, taking higher risk to build wealth over a long horizon.

questions.text: Why should irregular income (like bonuses) be treated carefully in budgeting?
options: It may not occur regularly and shouldn’t fund fixed commitments
It should always be spent fully
questions.explanation: Irregular income is uncertain and best used for one-time goals or debt reduction.

questions.text: Ethically communicating risk to clients requires:
options: Highlighting only high returns in presentations
Presenting both upside potential and downside risks clearly
questions.explanation: Balanced communication should clearly explain possible losses, volatility, and risk factors along with potential returns.

questions.text: Margin money in futures trading is primarily meant to:
options: Act as a down payment for ownership
Cover potential daily losses and ensure contract performance
questions.explanation: Margins are deposits to cover potential daily losses and ensure traders honour their obligations; they are adjusted daily via mark-to-market.

questions.text: The process of finding the present value from a known future value is called:
questions.explanation: Discounting is the reverse of compounding.

questions.text: All mutual fund distributors must hold a valid registration with:
questions.explanation: Distributors must obtain AMFI Registration Number (ARN) after completing the NISM Mutual Fund Distributors certification.

questions.text: Spread risk in credit markets is the risk that:
options: The yield difference between a corporate bond and a government bond of similar maturity widens
The difference between coupon and face value increases
The bid-ask spread in equity markets narrows
questions.explanation: Spread risk is the risk that the credit spread over government securities widens due to perceived higher risk, lowering bond prices.

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of mis-selling?
options: Explaining all risks clearly before sale
Selling a product unsuitable for the client’s risk profile to earn higher commission
questions.explanation: Mis-selling includes pushing unsuitable products mainly to earn higher commissions, ignoring client needs and risk profile.

questions.text: Which of the following is a secured loan?
questions.explanation: A home loan is backed by the property mortgaged to the lender.

questions.text: Under PMLA, intermediaries must report suspicious transactions to:
questions.explanation: The Financial Intelligence Unit–India (FIU-IND) under the Ministry of Finance receives suspicious transaction reports from intermediaries.

questions.text: Debt-to-income ratio (DTI) is computed as:
options: Monthly debt obligations ÷ Gross monthly income
questions.explanation: DTI assesses ability to service debt from monthly income.

questions.text: AIFs in India are regulated under:
questions.explanation: SEBI introduced the AIF Regulations in 2012 to bring all unregistered private pools such as PE, VC and hedge funds under a regulatory framework.

questions.text: Preferred shareholders generally have:
options: Priority over equity shareholders in dividend and liquidation but limited voting rights
Higher returns than equity in all circumstances
questions.explanation: Preference shareholders get fixed dividends and priority in liquidation but limited or no voting rights.

questions.text: Which of the following can accept demand deposits and issue cheques?
questions.explanation: Only banks can accept demand deposits and provide cheque facilities; NBFCs cannot.

questions.text: Sector funds must invest at least what percentage of total assets in the identified sector?
questions.explanation: Open-ended sector funds must invest at least 80% of total assets in equity and equity-related instruments of the specified sector.

questions.text: Lock-in period for investment in an Angel Fund portfolio company is at least:
questions.explanation: Investments by an Angel Fund in a portfolio company must be locked in for a minimum of three years.

questions.text: If monthly income ₹1 lakh and total EMIs ₹35,000, DTI ratio is:
Which of the following is an ethical way to communicate expected returns?
options: Guaranteeing a fixed return above FD rates
Showing past performance with clear disclaimers that returns are not guaranteed
Promising that losses will never occur
questions.explanation: Ethical communication must be balanced, factual, and include disclaimers that past performance does not guarantee future returns.

questions.text: To accumulate ₹10 lakh in 15 years at 9% p.a., the annual deposit required is approximately:
questions.explanation: Using FV of annuity formula, deposit ≈ 36,000 per year.

questions.text: Equity as an asset class represents:
options: A fixed claim on company’s assets and income
An ownership stake in a company
A loan given to the government
A derivative contract based on commodities
questions.explanation: Equity represents ownership in a company, with residual claim on assets and income after obligations to lenders are met.

questions.text: The investor’s ultimate record of ownership in mutual funds held in demat form is maintained by:
questions.explanation: In demat mode, the Depository Participant (DP) maintains the record of ownership under the investor’s demat account.

questions.text: From an adviser’s perspective, suitability of equity for a client depends on:
options: Risk tolerance, time horizon and financial goals
questions.explanation: Suitability assessment considers risk appetite, time horizon and objectives, not merely income or administrative details.

questions.text: The interest rate that includes all fees and charges to show total borrowing cost is called:
questions.explanation: APR reflects the true cost of borrowing including processing fees.

questions.text: Which is the MOST suitable investment for parking an emergency fund?
options: Liquid mutual fund or savings bank account
questions.explanation: Emergency funds must be readily accessible and low risk, so liquid funds or savings accounts are appropriate.

questions.text: AMFI primarily functions as:
options: A mutual fund industry self-regulatory organization (SRO)
questions.explanation: The Association of Mutual Funds in India (AMFI) is an SRO promoting investor awareness and ethical conduct among mutual funds.

questions.text: For arbitration of disputes between investors and brokers, the forum used is:
questions.explanation: Exchange arbitration panels handle disputes between investors and brokers as an alternative dispute resolution mechanism.

questions.text: Which of the following combinations correctly matches asset class and its typical characteristic?
options: Government bond – low credit risk, interest rate risk present
Real estate – highly liquid, intraday tradable
questions.explanation: Government bonds usually have low credit risk, but their prices are still affected by changes in interest rates.

questions.text: The financial life cycle typically starts with which stage?
questions.explanation: The financial life cycle begins when an individual starts earning and accumulating assets.

questions.text: In PMS, fixed cost refers to:
options: A variable charge based on profits
A percentage of assets under management payable regardless of performance
questions.explanation: Fixed cost is the management fee charged as a fixed percentage of AUM irrespective of performance.

questions.text: Circuit filters or price bands are imposed to:
options: Prevent extreme price movements in a single day
questions.explanation: Circuit filters cap daily price moves within a band to curb excessive volatility.

questions.text: “Investment-grade” debt generally refers to:
options: Debt rated in the lower categories indicating high default risk
Debt with credit ratings in higher categories indicating relatively lower default risk
Debt that has no rating but is issued by start-ups
Any government bond irrespective of rating
questions.explanation: Investment-grade ratings indicate relatively lower default risk compared to non–investment grade or ‘junk’ ratings.

questions.text: A person’s monthly income = ₹80,000, fixed expenses = ₹30,000, variable = ₹40,000. What’s monthly surplus?
Non-discretionary Portfolio Managers:
options: Require client approval for every transaction
Can invest only in government securities
questions.explanation: Non-discretionary Portfolio Managers act based on the client’s instructions for every investment decision.

questions.text: Which of these improves the current ratio (liquid assets ÷ current liabilities)?
questions.explanation: Reducing liabilities with existing cash improves ratio.

questions.text: Mark-to-market in futures trading means:
options: Adjusting contract value daily for changes in market price
Fixing profit at the start of the contract
questions.explanation: Mark-to-market involves daily settlement of profit or loss due to price movement, adjusting each participant’s margin account.

questions.text: SWP (Systematic Withdrawal Plan) is typically used by investors to:
options: Withdraw a fixed sum regularly from existing investments
questions.explanation: SWP enables investors to withdraw a fixed amount at regular intervals from their investment corpus.

questions.text: A derivative is a financial instrument whose value is derived from:
options: An underlying asset such as a stock, bond, commodity or index
questions.explanation: A derivative’s price depends on the value or performance of an underlying asset such as equity, bond, commodity, currency or index.

questions.text: Which of the following correctly pairs derivative type and user intent?
options: Option – limited loss for buyer; Future – symmetrical gains and losses
questions.explanation: Futures expose both sides to full price movement; option buyers have limited loss potential.

questions.text: A bond will trade at par value when:
options: Coupon rate is higher than required yield
Coupon rate equals the required yield to maturity
Coupon rate is lower than required yield
questions.explanation: If the bond’s coupon rate equals the market required yield for that maturity, the bond price equals its face (par) value.

questions.text: Which asset class is generally considered most suitable for capital preservation with modest returns over the short term?
options: Structured products linked to equity indices
questions.explanation: Liquid and short-term debt instruments usually focus on capital preservation and modest returns.

questions.text: Regulatory constraints are most likely to apply when:
options: The investor wants to invest abroad under LRS limits
The investor invests only in mutual funds
questions.explanation: Under RBI’s Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS), Indian residents can invest up to $250,000 overseas annually—this acts as a regulatory constraint.

questions.text: Online mutual fund transactions through MFU, BSE StAR, or NSE NMF II are processed by:
options: Exchange-backed platforms integrating RTAs and distributors
questions.explanation: Platforms like MF Utility, BSE StAR, and NSE NMF II are integrated systems connecting AMCs, RTAs, and intermediaries.

questions.text: The most widely used risk-adjusted performance measure is:
questions.explanation: The Sharpe Ratio is the most popular risk-adjusted performance measure, assessing excess return per unit of total risk.

questions.text: In a multi-cap fund, SEBI requires that at least 75% of assets are in equity with minimum allocation of:
options: 25% in large-cap, 25% in mid-cap, 25% in small-cap
questions.explanation: Multi-cap funds must invest at least 75% in equity-related instruments, with a minimum of 25% each in large, mid and small-cap stocks.

questions.text: Interval funds are:
options: Closed-end schemes that become open-ended during specified transaction periods
Schemes that can be bought only once a year
questions.explanation: Interval funds are a variant of closed-end funds that open for purchase and redemption at specified intervals for at least two days.

questions.text: A stock split means:
options: Company merges two shares into one
Company divides each share into smaller units to increase liquidity
Company issues new shares for cash
questions.explanation: A stock split divides shares into smaller units to make them more affordable and increase liquidity.

questions.text: The Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA), 2002 primarily aims to:
options: Curb generation and circulation of black money
questions.explanation: PMLA seeks to prevent money laundering and require reporting entities to maintain KYC and suspicious transaction records.

questions.text: According to Modern Portfolio Theory, portfolio risk is best measured by:
options: Variance or standard deviation of returns
questions.explanation: Markowitz demonstrated that variance (or standard deviation) of returns is a meaningful measure of portfolio risk.

questions.text: Equity is generally RECOMMENDED as part of a client’s portfolio because:
options: It enhances long-term growth potential despite short-term volatility
questions.explanation: Equity contributes to long-term growth in a diversified portfolio, though it carries higher short-term risk.

questions.case_text: Nisha has three loans — car loan ₹5 lakh at 11%, personal loan ₹3 lakh at 13%, and credit card outstanding ₹1 lakh at 36%. She considers consolidating them into a single loan at 12% for 4 years.

questions.text: Rakesh’s risk tolerance:
Short-term goal:
Investment horizon for retirement:
Suitable product for near-term goal:
Long-term goal allocation should favour:

questions.case_text: Sneha earns ₹80,000 per month. Her monthly household expense is ₹50,000, EMI ₹15,000, and she has health insurance of ₹3 lakh. She wants to know if her emergency fund and insurance coverage are adequate.

questions.case_text: Meera and Karan have a 10-year-old son and plan to save for his higher education, which they estimate will cost ₹25 lakh in 8 years. They can invest ₹20,000 per month in a balanced mutual fund expected to yield 9% per annum.

questions.case_text: Priya and Kunal are a salaried couple earning ₹9 lakh and ₹12 lakh per year respectively. They invest in ELSS and PPF and pay a home loan interest of ₹2.5 lakh annually. They want to optimise Section 80C and 24(b) benefits.

questions.text: Maximum 80C limit for each is:

Investment type offering 3-year lock-in under 80C:

questions.case_text: Riya earns ₹80,000 per month. Her fixed expenses are ₹30,000, variable ₹25,000, EMIs ₹15,000, and investments ₹5,000 per month. She has ₹3 lakh in liquid mutual funds.

questions.text: Monthly surplus/deficit is:

questions.text: Savings ratio per month is:

Her emergency fund is adequate?
options: No, should increase to 6 months of expenses
questions.explanation: Should hold ~₹3.3 lakh (6 × 55 k); she’s close but slightly short.

questions.case_text: Meera plans ₹25 lakh for her son’s higher studies in 9 years. She invests ₹17,000/month at 9% annual return.

questions.case_text: Ravi has ₹12 lakh annual income and loans: car loan ₹5 lakh @10%, home loan ₹30 lakh @8.5%. Total EMIs ₹45,000/month. He wants to take a ₹3 lakh personal loan for vacation.

questions.text: Current DTI ratio:
questions.explanation: 45k ÷ 1 lakh = 45%. Already high.

questions.text: Taking new loan will make DTI:
questions.explanation: New EMI increases DTI further.

questions.text: Should he take this loan?
questions.explanation: Borrowing for non-productive expense at high DTI is poor financial decision.

questions.text: A better choice would be to:
questions.explanation: Deferring until surplus is built is more prudent.

questions.text: His high DTI also affects:
questions.explanation: Higher debt burden and missed EMIs can lower credit rating.
